title: Behavioral Patterns & Risk Factors (Non-diagnostic, Educational)
notes: Patterns are not proof. Use them to generate questions, not conclusions.
Avoid profiling based on protected traits. Focus on behavior, context, and evidence.

patterns.title: Escalation Pattern
patterns.definition: Behavior increases in severity or frequency over time.
investigative_questions: Are there opportunity shifts (routine changes, access changes)?
Are multiple incidents actually linked or coincidental?
cautions: Escalation can be interrupted by external events; absence does not disprove linkage.

patterns.title: Signature vs Modus Operandi (Conceptual)
patterns.definition: MO is functional; signature is psychologically expressive (conceptual).
observables: Repeated functional steps (MO) may change with learning
Expressive elements may be more stable (but not guaranteed)
cautions: Do not over-interpret. Require corroboration across multiple domains.

patterns.title: Organized vs Disorganized Behavior (Simplified)
cautions: Real cases are mixed; avoid binary labels.
Scene messiness can reflect environment, not intent.

patterns.title: Repeat Location / Hotspot Pattern
patterns.definition: Incidents cluster in space/time due to opportunity structures.
observables: Similar time windows (end of month, weekends, late night)

patterns.title: Victim Selection Factors (Non-blaming)
patterns.definition: Selection may reflect access, exposure, or offender familiarity.
cautions: Focus on protective measures and support.

risk_domains.title: Individual-Level Factors (Contextual)
guardrails: Use only with strong evidence and fairness checks
